1.16 Year-scoped preservation workflow

preserve_years.py wraps byte preservation, full metadata snapshots, XMP extraction, image categorization and final verification for explicit year trees. Supply repeatable labeled source roots and one reference root:

uv run python preserve_years.py archives/years \
  --source-root archive-a=/media/archive-a/foto \
  --source-root archive-b=/media/archive-b/foto \
  --reference-root /media/reference/foto \
  --metadata-workers 4 --preservation-workers 2 \
  --metadata-backend rust --preservation-backend rust \
  --database-backend sqlite --metadata-shards 2

Only four-digit year directories under those supplied roots become tasks. This is not an automatic whole-volume intake. The source label becomes the archive namespace LABEL/YEAR and must remain stable on resume. The matching ledger prefers the same relative path, then a unique case-sensitive filename within the reference year; an ambiguous or missing reference causes full-original fallback. A match never bypasses the subsequent byte verification.

Option Purpose
--source-root LABEL=PATH Explicit source photo root; repeatable
--reference-root PATH Root containing corresponding reference years
--start-at LABEL/YEAR Skip earlier tasks only after their retained verification passes
--rate-mib N Preservation pacing budget
--metadata-workers N Native ExifTool budget; zero selects serial extraction
--preservation-workers N Byte-preservation pool, 1–36
--metadata-backend: rust, oxcaml Native extraction implementation
--preservation-backend: python, rust, oxcaml Byte/reconstruction implementation
--metadata-shards N Independent bounded extraction/compression owners
--database-backend: sqlite, turso Checkpoint engine
--sequential-pass Byte stage followed by metadata
--unified-pass Shared inventory with overlapping byte/metadata work; default

Unified mode lets metadata batches proceed only once the corresponding byte preservation has succeeded. Each stage retains its own checkpoint and database owner. It avoids a second independent inventory in the overlapping phases; it does not avoid reading whatever payloads are needed for actual identity proof.

The workflow records source/reference facts, matching decisions, tool hashes, compiler/extraction settings and available Git state in provenance. Tools are copied into the archive for reproducibility. Keep those artifacts with the payloads. A root-level summary is only the aggregate of its explicitly scoped years, not certification of unrelated lrmobile folders, other volumes or an entire Lightroom library.

A retained archive created by the former hardcoded volume workflow has different scope metadata. Resume it with its archived producing tools or use a new generic output directory; do not silently replace its old scope with newly supplied roots. A same-looking year label does not establish the same source inventory.
